Where I got to
I reconstructed the tree from dump.txt and verified it file-by-file with SHA-256: 371 files clean, the only two mismatches being export.sh (it embeds its own file marker, so my parser truncates it) and LICENSE (elided by design). Two things came out of that verification that you should see before anything else.

Session drift, caught again — three slices this time. My session memory opened believing the tree was at Slice 54 with an unverified ~1250 baseline. The tree is at Slice 57 (likes: schema and data access, 0008_menu_item_reactions.sql). That's now the fourth time the SHA-256 reconstruction has caught this, which continues to justify the ritual.

The baseline is 1273, verified two independent ways. Your terminal log shows total: 1273, failed: 0 on both the Debug and the Release run, plus 20/20 end-to-end. I rebuilt the arithmetic from the tree and it reproduces exactly: 921 [Fact] + 329 [InlineData] + 17 KeyRelations + 6 KeyColumnsAddedByAlter = 1273. A naive grep gives 330 [InlineData]; the 330th is inside a comment in ProfileDetailsTests.cs. Everything is green — ci_local.sh --with-all --with-e2e passed all nine gates.

What I chose to build, and why that order
The plan names Stage 5b as next: two surfaces, no remaining decisions. I split it, and took the guest's like control (§11.1) first rather than the administrator's count (§11.4). Three reasons: the plan itself calls the write-with-no-caller "the stronger of the two" open obligations; the administrator's count has nothing to count until a guest can press, so shipping it first renders a column no surface can populate; and only the guest surface can produce a press, so an end-to-end scenario is writable in this slice and can then be extended by the count slice.

I'm also including the scenario in the same slice rather than deferring it — that's F-106's lesson applied on the first opportunity. Four slices of picture work shipped with no scenario, and a ValidationMessage outside its EditForm answered HTTP 500 on every decorated item the whole time.

A finding, found on the way in
F-112. F-89 ruled that MinimumCountedClasses should be the only place the §16.4 counted-class census is written, deleting two prose copies. The doc comment on that constant has since grown a narrative census of its own — "twelve, sixteen, eighteen, nineteen … twenty-five, and now twenty-seven" — while the constant one line below it reads 29, and the true census computed from §16.4 is 32. So the copy F-89 preserved now holds two numbers, neither of which is the census. That's F-89's shape recurring inside F-89's own repair, which is the same evidence-beats-ruling pattern F-89 itself invoked.

What's authored so far
TableOrderSurface.razor — both reaction services injected; _likedByMe read beside the pictures in LoadMenuAsync; ToggleLikeAsync applying the write's own IsLiked rather than the tap's intent; the control rendered in the detail panel, with the mechanical reason recorded (a <button> inside a <button> is not markup a parser keeps — the card would split and its name-bearing half would stop staging).
app.css — .order-menu-detail-actions and .order-menu-like*, --touch-target floor, state carried by glyph shape as well as colour, no new breakpoint.
Still to author
MenuItemReactionSurfaceContractTests (4 facts, one of which computes its subject over Components/Pages/Table/ to hold Stage 5a's staff-only count ruling); the harness reader/presser; scenario 21 in a new MenuReactionScenarios.cs; SeatGuestAsync moved into TableJourneys with EndToEndScenarios keeping a one-line private forwarder that supplies its own patience constant; and all five documents.

Predicted count: 1273 → 1278 (+4 contract facts, +1 scenario); §16.3 goes 20 → 21; the §16.4 census 32 → 33 and the floor moves with it.

I ran out of tool budget mid-authoring, so I have no archive to hand you yet. Say the word and I'll finish the remaining files and package the .tar.gz — full files, repo-relative paths, explicit delete list, git add lines for the new files.

The arithmetic closed exactly
I recomputed the count from the edited tree rather than carrying my prediction: 926 [Fact] + 329 [InlineData] + 17 + 6 = 1278, which is the number I predicted before authoring. The e2e project holds 21 facts, matching the §16.3 suite going 20 → 21. The §16.4 census computes to 33 and the floor is set to 33 — no disagreement between any count §16.4 claims and the file it names.

What shipped
Stage 5b-i — §11.1's like control. In the item's detail panel, discharging the stronger of the two obligations Stage 5a re-opened (a write with no caller) plus one of the two reads. I took the guest's control before §11.4's count deliberately: a count surface shipped first would be a read with no writer — the same defect inverted and harder to see, because the column renders correctly and every number on it is zero.

The placement was predicted; the failure mode was not. The plan said the control belongs in the panel because "a second interactive element inside a button is not markup this application can write." True, and one register short of the useful reason: the HTML parser doesn't reject a nested button, it repairs it — closing the outer element, so the card becomes two pieces and the half carrying the dish's name stops staging anything. Nothing throws, the Razor compiles, no bUnit renders it, and the 375px barrier measures where controls are rather than whether they still work. That's now a test rather than a sentence.

Two of Stage 5a's rulings stopped being paragraphs. The count is staff-facing; a reaction publishes nothing. Each was one line from being improved into a defect — a span on a card, or a forwarding verb whose symptom is load rather than an error on every phone in the building.

Scenario 21 ships with the control, not a slice later. That's F-109 applied on its first opportunity against a control with F-106's exact profile. The reload is the whole scenario: everything before it is satisfied by a bool on a component no database hears about.

F-112 — the §16.4 census was written three times inside the one place F-89's ruling had cleared, and two of the three were wrong. Narrative deleted, floor 29 → 33, no gate (F-89's own reasoning).

One thing that changed during authoring, worth flagging
The count-prohibition gate's first draft keyed on the bare identifier ListLikeCountsAsync and failed against my own tree — the file that must not call it is also the natural place to write down why. Both keys now carry an open parenthesis: the rule is about a call, and a call can't omit its parens. F-67's shape.

Verification
All four contract facts were emulated against the edited tree and each proven sensitive by a planted defect — nesting the control is caught by two facts at once, deleting it reads as a count of zero, redirecting the guest's read to the count trips both the prohibition and the vacuity guard, and a SetLikedAsync mention in MenuWorkflow is named. Markdown table gate clean across 25 documents; version gate clean on both versioned documents (44 entries, strictly descending); Razor tag-tree and brace balance confirmed; byte hygiene clean across all 13 files.

Nothing was compiled or run. The four specific risks are ranked in _CHANGES.md — the scenario's aria-pressed wait is the largest, since a slow re-render fails as a timeout about the harness rather than a wrong answer about the product.

Three veto points are written out with reversion instructions: the SeatGuestAsync move into the harness, the deliberate absence of an in-flight press guard, and the floor moving without a gate to keep it moving.
